In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods to improve the accuracy and efficiency of macromolecular refinement.
developing a method for the refinement of structures containing nucleic acid residues.
the construction of a dictionary for the refinement of DNA and RNA structures at atomic resolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dictionary provides a good basis for the refinement of structures with nucleic acids, but further work is needed to improve the refinement of the backbone torsional parameters.
the new nucleic acid dictionary improves the refinement of nucleosides, nucleotides and nucleic acid structures.
the new nucleic acid parameters provide a significant improvement in the refinement of nucleotide-containing structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new dictionary has the potential to improve refinement of nucleic acids and nucleic acid-protein structures, and that the dictionary is useful in refinement at atomic resolution (1.2-1.5 A) as well as at high resolution (1.0 A).
the new dictionary is more reliable and provides more accurate parameters than the previous one, which was based on only 12 structures.
the dictionary provides a better description of the structures than previous dictionaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the refinement of nucleotides in protein-nucleic acid complexes is not significantly different than the refinement of nucleotide in nucleic acid structures.
the refinement parameters for nucleic acids can be improved significantly using a larger sample of refined structures.
a dictionary of nucleic acid structures should be used in refinement trials.
